Range Lab

GTO poker solver and trainer · 2–9 players · 10–100bb

Push / Fold Nash

Every player either folds or moves all-in; facing a shove you fold or call. Chip-EV equilibrium with card removal.

Players
10bb

Push/fold is the right model up to about 15bb. Deeper than that, use the Preflop tab.

With payouts, every decision maximises prize-pool equity instead of chips, and EVs are shown in % of the prize pool. Everyone at the table is assumed to be everyone left in the tournament.

How this is solved

External-sampling Monte Carlo CFR over the 169 starting-hand classes. Each iteration deals real cards, so card removal between players is exact.

Heads-up and three-way all-ins use precomputed equity tables (150k and 3k samples per matchup). All-ins with four or more players run out a random board.

Hands near the indifference line often show mixed frequencies. Their EV gap is tiny, so either action is fine in practice.

Preflop solver

Open, 3-bet, 4-bet and all-in ranges for every position. Pots that reach the flop are scored with an equity-realization model.

Players
100bb
Bet sizing

3-bets add one extra open-size per caller. A raise above 42% of the stack becomes an all-in. Facing a 4-bet, the only raise is all-in.

Postflop realization model

When a hand sees a flop, each player's share of the pot is their equity times a realization factor, then normalized. Deeper stacks (higher SPR) widen the factors.

Single-raised and limped pots
3-bet pots and bigger

Taken from pots that see a flop or go all-in (no flop, no drop).

How this is solved

The full preflop betting tree for all players is solved with external-sampling Monte Carlo CFR on real dealt cards. All-ins are scored with exact equity tables (heads-up and three-way) or a random runout (four or more players).

Postflop play is not solved here. Pots that reach the flop are split by realized equity, which depends on position, who raised last, hand playability and stack-to-pot ratio. Tune these under Postflop realization model. To study a flop exactly, open a heads-up flop node and send it to the Postflop tab.

All players start with the same stack. Antes are dead money.

Heads-up postflop

Solve a single flop, turn or river spot between two ranges with discounted CFR. Card removal is exact.

Bet sizes (% of pot)

Solving stops when exploitability drops below the target or the iteration cap is reached. Each extra flop size roughly doubles flop solve time.

How this is solved

Vectorized discounted CFR over every combo in both ranges, with exact card removal and exact showdowns. Exploitability is measured with a full best response.

Turn and river spots are solved exactly. A full three-street flop tree needs gigabytes of memory, so flop solves cover flop and turn betting, and the river card is dealt and checked down.

Range syntax: 22+, A2s+, KTo+, QJs, T9s:0.5, AhKh. A weight after the colon is a frequency.

Hand review

Paste hand histories from PokerStars, GGPoker or another site with the same text format. Each of your preflop decisions is graded against the Preflop tab’s solve.

How hands are matched

Seats are matched by distance from the button, so hands from any table size can be graded against a solve with a different player count. Players in seats the solve doesn’t have (UTG at a 9-handed table against a 6-handed solve) must fold before anyone else acts, or the hand is skipped. Seats the table doesn’t have count as folds.

Raise sizes are matched to the nearest size in the solve, and big raises to an all-in. Only preflop is graded. A note appears when the hand’s effective stack is far from the solve’s depth.

Pasted text stays in this page. It is not saved.
